secret-enemies-of-true-republicanism-mos:
Andrew B. Smolnikar published this long treatise at Springhill, Pennsylvania, in 1859. Smolnikar had spent eighteen years as a Benedictine monk and a crown professor of Bible studies before leaving that life in 1838. He held that signs and forecasts had named him a herald of a new age.

Smolnikar argues that hidden foes block true republican rule and stir up wars and revolts. His plan would free nations from kings and harsh rule, then bring lasting peace and fairness to the whole globe. The book blends faith, forecasts, and politics in a call for a world remade.
unitarianism-in-america-a-history-of-its:
George Willis Cooke wrote Unitarianism in America to trace where the movement began in the United States, how it organized itself, and what it achieved. In his preface he says the obscure New England beginnings deserved fuller treatment than they had yet received, though his space forced him to keep that part brief. He likewise touches only lightly on the church fights that split the Unitarians from the older Congregational body.

Cooke names the writers he means to supplement rather than replace. They include George E. Ellis on the half century of controversy, Joseph Henry Allen on the liberal movement, William Channing Gannett's memoir of Ezra Stiles Gannett, and John White Chadwick on old and new beliefs. Readers get a survey built to fill gaps in those earlier works, with stress on institutions and growth rather than on doctrine alone.
